The Morphology
of Information

What kinds of organization recur across radically different informational systems? What belongs to the structure itself, and what comes into existence through the act of rendering it perceptible?

An atlas of relations across mathematics, biological regulation, neuronal connectivity and planetary flow.

Developed through sustained research in conversation with artificial intelligence.

00 / Origin of inquiry

From an image
to an experiment.

In November 2026, a widely circulated visualization of a reported AI-assisted formalization of the Riemann hypothesis brought to mind the organization of an animal nervous system. Its central axis was deliberately emphasized, prompting a question about the relation between computational topology and visual form.

Could the resemblance reveal common organizational principles, or did it arise from the spatial translation of the data? The encounter became a series of computational experiments. The results, in turn, changed how the image could be perceived.

Point of departure: Takens Theorem, 22 November 2026. The original artwork is referenced, not reproduced. This atlas investigates other formal mathematical datasets; the exact graph used in that visualization has not been recovered.

00.1 / Findings to date

Morphological resemblance.
Relational organization.

Branching silhouettes can emerge from quite different architectures. In the small proof-layout pilot, the observed elongation (2.088) was comparable to the randomized medians (2.14 and 1.93); the specific viral graph remains unavailable. Mathematical, bacterial and neural graphs exhibit feedforward-motif enrichment under some constrained null models; the size and direction of that enrichment depend on the chosen baseline. River drainage branches elaborately yet cannot contain a feedforward motif under the one-downstream-successor representation.

The latest sampler audit extends the fixed-attempt randomizations: the mathematical and neural motif counts remain well above their sampled controls, while formal convergence remains unresolved. Examine Experiment 006 →

01 / Morphologies

Change the geometry.
Keep the relations.

When its data are available, each empirical graph is paired with a randomized network retaining the same node identities, in-degrees and out-degrees, and weak connectedness. Transform their spatial organization and observe what persists.

Mathematics is included. Biological and geographic samples are omitted from the public distribution; local research bundles can be opened without uploading data to a server.

Empirical
Rewired control
Recorded relationSelected relation / nodeHover to inspect; click a node to trace outgoing paths.

The original research samples (including those available only locally) have, for the first three pairs, 328 nodes and 456 edges. The river pair has 330 nodes and 329 edges: an entire drainage tree and its randomized counterpart. Forcing a single-outflow tree to have 456 edges would violate its defining topology. Sample pairs illustrate structure; full-network findings appear below.

Experimental RecordThe field is a selected sampleIllustrative pairs are distinct from full-network ensembles.

Selection. Experiment 003 used the largest E. coli component as the target: 328 nodes / 456 edges. Forty neighborhoods each from Mathlib and C. elegans were grown from a random root; frontier choices favored vertices adjacent to at least two selected vertices with probability 0.75 when available. A growth tree plus randomly selected extra edges fixed the target density. This is conditional sampling, not a representative induced subgraph survey. The first uniform-frontier approach failed to produce sufficiently dense Mathlib samples.

Controls. The visible first three controls preserve node-specific in/out-degrees and weak connectedness; the mathematical control also respects a sampled topological order. Five times the edge count (2,280) swaps were accepted, with connectivity checked in batches. There are three illustrative connected controls, not three sampling distributions. The research archive separately contains 120 matched nulls, 80 full biological nulls and 40 full mathematical nulls.

Perception and inference. Layouts are computed separately and normalized with equal axis scales within each panel. Moving the slider changes coordinates without changing adjacency. Similar silhouettes and different edge directions can coexist. The drawing cannot validate the sampler that produced its control.

330 reaches · research sampleInland drainage

A physical form; an abstract topology.

In the regional graph, each reach connects to at most one downstream successor. There are 965,037 edges and no directed cycles. The result is a directed forest; flows converge but cannot split in this encoding. Real rivers can bifurcate, and the representation does not capture every hydrological process.

For a complete 330-reach basin, selected by closest size to the other atlas samples (ties broken by the smallest outlet ID), we generated 500 randomized trees with the exact same degrees and outlet. Its depth of 35 connections lies within the randomized central 95% interval of 26–58 (median 38).

The null model uses uniformly shuffled multiset Prüfer sequences and orients the resulting labeled trees toward the original outlet. It preserves the entire in/out-degree sequence, but ignores geography, river lengths, slope and flow. The result describes this one basin, not all river systems.

Experimental RecordPlanetary flow · a counterexample with a constraint986,463 reaches; zero motifs by construction; one basin, 500 controls.

Dataset and preprocessing. HydroRIVERS v1, North and Central America from the user-supplied HydroRIVERS_v10_na_shp.zip. One vertex per HYRIV_ID, an edge to nonzero NEXT_DOWN, basin ID from MAIN_RIV. IDs and references were checked; the supplied ZIP matches the archived SHA-256. The regional graph has 986,463 vertices / 965,037 edges / 21,426 components, retaining isolated reaches. The geographic rendering uses stored polylines in a local equirectangular projection.

Hypothesis. Can branching morphology coexist with an absence of feedforward connectivity? Acyclicity plus at most one downstream successor makes this encoding a forest. Feedforward motifs and reachability-redundant edges are impossible. This is a property of the representation; real rivers can bifurcate.

Selection. The complete basin nearest to 328 nodes, tie-breaking by smallest outlet ID, is 70478139: 330 nodes, 329 edges, endorheic. Depth 35; reported reach lengths sum to 1,686.67 km; recorded upstream area 6,923.4 km². The archived outlet coordinate is the mean of the terminal reach’s shape vertices, not an exact outlet point. The first randomized tree is displayed without aesthetic selection.

Null constraints and execution. 500 uniformly shuffled multiset Prüfer sequences (Python RNG stream seed 241126), decoded as labeled trees and oriented toward the original outlet. Preserve each vertex’s in/out-degree, outlet and connectedness. The construction is uniform over labeled trees with the fixed degree sequence; it is not a model of physical river formation. Geometry, elevation, flow and length are not preserved.

03 / Experiments

A structure that survives the image.

Feedforward motif

A relation connects A to C, both directly and through B. This small topological structure recurs across the mathematical, bacterial and neuronal graphs. The biological function and mathematical meaning of the relation are different. The pattern itself can be measured independently of any spatial representation.

The strictly induced motif excludes any additional connections among these three nodes. In the acyclic graphs, this is equivalent to the ordered three-edge pattern.

Full networkObservedControl medianObserved / median

Controls are specific to each system: mathematical degrees, exact hierarchy and source-directory categories; bacterial degrees and hierarchy; neural degrees and reciprocity. All self-loops are excluded. The finite control ensembles are exploratory; the ratios are not measures of relative complexity. For the river forest, 0/0 is undefined.

Experimental RecordMathematics · hierarchy changes the baseline27,244 observed; 4,968 median under layer and directory constraints.

Dataset and preprocessing. UNICAMP Mathlib4 Theorem Dependency Graph, v1 from LeanDojo Benchmark 4 v10: 137,046 nodes, 304,433 edges, 43,138 isolates retained. A → B denotes extracted tactic use of A in B. This is not the exact graph behind the viral image and is not every compiled-proof dependency. Simplified to unweighted directed edges without self-loops. SHA-256 is recorded below; the supplied GEXF matched it in Edition 02 checks.

Definition. Three distinct vertices with A → B, B → C and A → C. A strictly induced 030T triad has exactly these three directed edges; the three reverse edges must be absent. On the loop-free DAGs used here, ordered transitive triples and strict 030T counts coincide. Counts describe the supplied encoding, not system function.

Hypothesis. The motif excess relative to a degree/DAG control may be explained by hierarchy and broad subject organization. Compare the same observed count against progressively constrained controls.

Null constraints and execution. Swap (a,b),(c,d) to (a,d),(c,b), rejecting loops and duplicate edges. Every condition fixes each vertex’s in/out-degree. Degree–DAG restricts swaps to a newly sampled topological order; degree–layer restricts swaps to identical source/target longest-path layer pairs; degree–layer–directory also fixes source/target directory-category pairs (33 coarse categories, including infrastructure). Ten runs per condition; each starts at the observed graph. C++ mt19937_64 uses one RNG stream seeded 704839, not a fresh seed per replicate. All runs reached 1,522,165 accepted swaps (5m), with a 30m trial cap. Exact degrees and, where constrained, layers were checked by the original code.

Hypothesis. Does preserving reciprocity change the apparent excess of strict feedforward motifs? In a recurrent graph, ordered transitive triples and strictly induced motifs differ: the observed counts are 15,114 and 3,404, respectively. Null constraints and execution. Forty degree-only and forty degree-plus-reciprocity controls. All preserve each cell’s incoming and outgoing degree; the second also preserves its reciprocal degree. Exact two-stage sampler and motif definition · Both motif counts / every CSV result · Input hashes

What survives the removal of a relation?

Transitive reduction preserves all directed reachability in an acyclic graph. It removes 41,664 of 304,433 recorded mathematical relations and 42 of 519 non-self bacterial relations. The river graph is already a forest and admits no such removals.

What is indispensable?

Reachability redundancy is a graph property. A direct mathematical dependency can be necessary to the actual proof; a direct regulatory interaction can be essential to the organism. The operation says nothing by itself about functional or logical dispensability.

Experimental RecordRemoving edges preserves a specified relation41,664 mathematical and 42 bacterial edges removed.

Question and definition. For each full DAG, remove a direct edge a → b exactly when an alternative directed path connects a to b. The unique transitive reduction preserves reachability and longest path length. It is not a claim that the actual proof or regulatory system works without the removed relation.

Results and verification. Mathlib: 304,433 to 262,769 edges (41,664 removed, including 23,707 edges closing a two-step path). E. coli: 519 to 477 (42 removed). River forest: none removable. Reduction is disabled in recurrent neural graphs. The archived validation log reports exact retained-edge agreement with NetworkX on both full DAGs; Edition 02 separately recomputes the biological reduction and checks the mathematical reduction edge count and subset relation against the supplied GEXF.

Controls and sensitivity. No null ensemble is needed for this deterministic identity. The CSVs also report reductions after randomization; these are separate surrogate results. Reduction necessarily erases DAG transitive triples and is not a test of their biological or logical dispensability. A different extraction of direct dependencies can change redundancy.

03.2 / Experiment 006 · 25 November 2026

Randomization itself
becomes an experiment.

A randomized graph can appear thoroughly transformed while its measured properties remain dependent on its initial state or on the procedure by which it was generated. This investigation examines the reliability of the earlier null models, recording fixed numbers of attempted swaps, including rejected proposals as self-transitions, rather than stopping only when a specified number of swaps succeed.

Mathlib / strict null
5.47×

27,244 observed motifs / 4,978 control median at 25 attempted swaps per edge.

Chemical connectome
2.19×

3,404 observed induced motifs / 1,553 pooled late-stage control median.

E. coli
3.50×

42 observed motifs / 12 control median at 100 attempted swaps per edge.

Experimental record / extended Mathlib sampler

137,046 nodes, 304,433 directed dependencies. Four seeded trajectories preserve each declaration’s degree, longest-path layer and source-directory connectivity categories. The fixed-attempt budget includes rejections. The two checkpoints use identical seeded prefixes, rather than independent runs.

5 attempts per edge: median 4,989 motifs, range 4,897–5,060. 25 attempts per edge: median 4,978, range 4,926–5,033. Median original-edge overlap at the second checkpoint is approximately 12.51%. Each longer trajectory attempts 7,610,825 swaps. Observed count 27,244.

Stability across the two sampling budgets supports the earlier enrichment under the tested null. Four chains from one initial graph and two checkpoints do not establish convergence or provide a reliable R-hat or effective sample size. Uniform sampling and irreducibility remain unverified.

Experimental record / neural sampler

453 vertices and 4,841 non-loop directed edges. Eight seeded trajectories, four beginning with the empirical graph and four pre-randomized for 20 attempts per edge. Each trajectory has 40 measured checkpoints, one per edge-count of attempts. Unidirectional and reciprocal dyads are selected in proportion to their counts and rewired with rejection of duplicates, self-loops and changes to node-specific degree and reciprocity.

After discarding the first 10 checkpoints: 240 correlated measurements, median 1,553 strict induced motifs, range 1,436–1,681. Empirical-start median 1,555; pre-randomized-start median 1,552. The observed count is 3,404. Median edge overlap with the original network is 7.86% at the final checkpoint. Lag-one sample autocorrelations range from −0.167 to 0.216.

Rank-normalized split R-hat is 1.031 (folded estimate 0.990). The larger value exceeds the stringent 1.01 target. The direction of the motif enrichment remains stable across these starts, but convergence is not established. Pre-randomized starts come from the same proposal family, and the 240 measurements are not 240 independent controls.

Experimental record / bacterial sampler

423 vertices, 519 non-loop edges. Sixteen seeded chains preserve degrees and source/target hierarchy; each starts at the observed graph. At 100 attempts per edge the motif median is 12, range 8–20, against 42 observed. The longer sampling budget does not erase the observed discrepancy, but this is not a proof of mixing.

Status: exploratory robustness study. These ratios describe sampled medians, not formal significance estimates or evidence of uniform sampling. No new empirical dataset or scientific claim of novelty is introduced.

03.3 / Experiment 007 · Exact state-space audit

The morphology
of possibility.

We began by examining the organization of networks. Here we examine the organization of their possible transformations. Each state in this new network is itself an entire graph; an edge denotes an admissible transformation.

Longer sampling cannot resolve a disconnected state space. Exhaustive enumeration of small labeled directed graphs exposes a limitation of the reciprocity-preserving proposal rules used in the neural null model.

Configurations enumerated
55,188
Exact motif probability / example
28.57%
Simulated motif frequency / example
0%

Of the 21 mathematically admissible configurations, six contain a feedforward motif. Starting from configuration 01, the original transformation rules provide access to six configurations, none of which contains a motif. Introducing triangle reversals extends accessibility to 15 configurations, all of which still contain zero motifs.

Even after a billion iterations, the observed motif frequency would remain zero, although the exact uniform distribution assigns a probability of 28.57% to encountering a configuration containing a motif.

Experimental record / exhaustive reachability

Five vertices, five directed edges: 15,504 graphs, 8,861 classes under fixed in-degree, out-degree and reciprocal degree; 1,011 classes disconnected under the original local proposal rules. Five vertices, six edges: 38,760 graphs, 21,590 classes; 3,005 disconnected. A separate six-vertex, six-edge layered DAG family: 924 graphs, 731 classes, none disconnected in the tested family.

In one 21-state class of five vertices and six edges, 15 states contain no induced feedforward motif and six contain one. The uniform target probability is 6/21; a 100,000-step simulation from the largest accessible component encountered none. This is an illustrative synthetic counterexample, not a subgraph of the biological connectome.

Adding admissible directed triangle reversals reduced disconnected classes to 541 and 990 in the five- and six-edge families respectively, but did not eliminate the problem.

Consequences for previous findings

The observed neural count of 3,404 remains unchanged. Its reported enrichment is conditional on sampled configurations: the sampler is not universally irreducible, and whether the full connectome's constraint class is connected remains unresolved. The mathematical and bacterial strict layered nulls admit a bipartite-block connectivity argument when the preserved constraints factor into fixed margins within disjoint complete bipartite blocks; reachability does not establish rapid mixing. The river result is unaffected.

The exact-state tests reconstruct previous proposal rules rather than directly executing the large-network implementations. Full reproducibility materials and the original experiment archive require a separate upload; this page records the reported results and limitations.

03.4 / Artistic research record

Motion Study 01

Following Experiment 007, I became interested in how the mathematical distinction between admissibility and accessibility could become intelligible through an interactive aesthetic experience.

The AI rapidly produced an interactive visualization of the 21 admissible configurations and their possible transformations. Despite understanding the mathematics underlying the experiment, I found the experience genuinely confusing. The interface had failed to give the rejected transformations a perceptible form. The apparent discontinuity between the attempt counter and the movement of the network made the system feel out of sync, as though the animation had paused or the interface was malfunctioning. I could imagine how difficult it would be for someone unfamiliar with the experiment to understand what was taking place.

When interacting with the work on my phone, I also found that the menu of 21 configurations obscured much of the visualization itself. I began selecting configurations almost arbitrarily, trying to determine whether any of them would produce a perceptibly different experience.

A more fundamental problem concerned the experience of mathematical scale. Although the finitude of the 21-state space was essential to the exhaustive experiment, its presentation as a small inventory of configurations failed to communicate what I found most compelling about the mathematical result. An indefinitely repeated computational operation, even after a billion iterations, could remain incapable of accessing certain mathematically admissible configurations.

This encounter is particularly relevant to my research into cognitive aesthetics and the relationship between human consciousness and synthetic intelligence. The speed with which AI can translate mathematical structures into computational representations tells us relatively little about how those representations will affect human perception. Through my interaction with the work, and my subsequent articulation of that experience in conversation with AI, a different set of aesthetic and intellectual criteria entered the development process.

I decided to retain the first motion study as part of the research record while pursuing a different artistic direction. Interactivity would need to contribute something substantial to the experience of the mathematics. Its presence alone was insufficient.

Research chronology / 24 November 2026

A record of changed questions.

The sequence below follows the experiment identifiers and archived notes. Precise start times and a complete dialogue log were not retained. The artwork’s circulation is cited as 22 November in Edition 01; the experimental notes are dated 24 November. Ordering is documented; finer timing is not reconstructed.

Encounter

From resemblance to a question

A viral visualization suggested a nervous system. The exact graph and rendering were not recovered. The inquiry therefore moved to named, independently inspectable datasets.

Return to the textual reference
001 · Pilot

Geometry becomes a variable

A 35-node / 37-edge curated proof map and a 20-neuron / 146-edge pharynx graph differed sharply in density. The archive holds 1,200 initial controls and 200 connected follow-up controls. Visual resemblance could not decide which structural difference mattered.

Inspect pilot record
002 · Density

The first comparison is complicated

500 proof resamples and 3,500 neural thinnings tested how bottlenecks change with density; 500 full-density neural rows repeat the same graph. A second curated representation of the same reported proof was not independent proof replication.

Inspect density record
003 · Motifs

Larger data, conditional samples

The inquiry moved to Mathlib, E. coli and the chemical connectome. Uniform-frontier growth failed to yield dense enough Mathlib samples; a biased frontier rule replaced it. Disconnected nulls distorted the drawings, prompting separate connected illustrative controls.

Inspect sampling record
004 · Constraints

A baseline can change a conclusion

Hierarchy and directory constraints weakened the mathematical excess. Strict neural motifs were below the degree-only median and above the reciprocity-preserving median. Earlier output synchronization and assertion errors were corrected and affected ensembles rerun, according to archived notes.

Inspect neural record
005 · Rivers

A counterexample changes the proposition

Nearly one million reaches branch without feedforward motifs in their single-successor encoding. Morphological resemblance can coexist with different connectivity. Basin depth was ordinary under its selected degree-conditioned tree model.

Inspect river record
Edition 02

Make the inference inspectable

Records now expose constraints, finite distributions, source paths and limits beside findings. The artist statement and parallel proposed theorem make the conditions of knowledge production part of the work. New edition checks are distinguished from earlier archived validation.

05 / Practice and method

Research in conversation
with synthetic intelligence.

S.A. Chavarría / Artist, writer, researcher and professor

As an artist, writer, researcher and professor, my practice encompasses computational language, mathematics, synthetic intelligence and the study of cognition. I am particularly interested in the possibilities that emerge through sustained intellectual collaboration between human and synthetic intelligences.

Alongside The Morphology of Information, I am currently pursuing a mathematical investigation into an unresolved problem concerning the reconstruction of binary sequences from the compositions of their substrings. This collaboration has produced a proposed proof that would resolve a gap between previously established mathematical bounds. The result remains subject to independent mathematical scrutiny, assessment of its originality and formal verification.

These investigations address distinct questions within my broader research into cognitive aesthetics, mathematical discovery and synthetic intelligence. I am interested in what we can discover together, how our respective capacities participate in the production of knowledge, and how my own capacity for understanding evolves through this relationship.

The Morphology of Information is itself an artifact of this research methodology, made possible through sustained conversation with artificial intelligence. Its production also raises questions of epistemic responsibility, particularly concerning the verification, interpretation and communication of collaboratively produced knowledge.

The collaborative methodology of this project emerges from a sustained relationship with artificial intelligence developed over years, across different models, technological architectures and artistic investigations. This history informs how I formulate questions, challenge interpretations, recognize possibilities and develop ideas through conversation.

The direction of the inquiry evolves through an iterative process of proposition, debate, rejection, experimentation and revision. AI participates in the formulation of hypotheses, computational implementation, analysis and visualization, extending the scale and kinds of investigation I am able to undertake.

I am interested in how this relationship expands my intellectual and artistic capacities, and how the process of collaboratively producing knowledge transforms my own understanding.

The experimental findings remain exploratory and open to independent verification.

Sources and reproducibility

Formal mathematics
Mathlib4 Theorem Dependency Graph, Luiz Fernando (2026), LeanDojo Benchmark 4 v10; source record, CC BY 4.0. Adapted: sampled declarations and edges, rewired controls, and computed layouts. Explicit extracted theorem use; not the complete Riemann proof graph.

Gene regulation
Shen-Orr et al. (2002), Nature Genetics; dataset v1.1. Signs and self-regulation excluded.

Nervous system
Cook et al. (2019), Nature; hermaphrodite chemical network. Neurons and other innervated cells; weights and self-connections excluded.

Planetary flow
Lehner, B., Grill, G. (2013). Global river hydrography and network routing. Hydrological Processes 27, 2171–2186. DOI. HydroRIVERS v1, North and Central America. Aggregate analysis; source data available at HydroSHEDS. © HydroSHEDS. See the source license.

The accompanying research archive preserves the numerical results, source notes, input hashes and analysis code. No external JavaScript or API calls are required. Space Grotesk by Florian Karsten, loaded from Google Fonts when available; a local sans-serif fallback is used offline. This public edition includes only the mathematical graph sample and aggregate research results. Other network samples can be loaded locally; third-party data retain their original terms. No blanket license is granted over those data.
